B: Hello.
A: Hello. Darren.
B: Abena. Hi.
A: All right.
B: So. Where are you?
A: King's Lynn.
B: Okay. I'm in Crawley. Near Gatwick.
A: Right. Planes, then.
B: Everyone says that. Yes, planes. You stop noticing.
A: Like the factory. You stop smelling the peas after a bit.
B: Peas?
A: Frozen veg plant. I run the lines. Blanchers, packing.
B: Okay. Long hours?
A: Twelve-hour shifts. Four on, four off. More in the season.
B: Twelve hours on your feet, that's a lot.
A: That's all right. You get used to it. What's yours?
B: Pharmacy technician. Three days a week. I dispense, check the prescriptions before the pharmacist signs, and spend half my life on the phone to GP receptionists telling them the script is wrong.
A: Do they listen?
B: Eventually. If you're firm. If you're nice, they put you on hold.
A: Same with the office lot at ours. Managers come down with a clipboard, no idea what they're looking at, tell you to speed the line up. I tell them no, the seals ain't right, that's not going out.
B: Good. And they don't like it.
A: No. That's cost me team leader twice.
B: Honestly, I'd take that over being team leader. I clash with my area manager about rotas all the time, and I said to him, I'm not doing management, I'm not chasing people about rotas all day.
A: No. More trouble than it's worth.
B: Exactly.
A: You got kids, then? You said three days.
B: Two. Thirteen and nine. When the little one goes to secondary, I'll do more hours. Right now school wants money for something every week, so I probably should anyway.
A: Yeah.
B: You?
A: No. Just me. My mum's up the road, I do her garden. Her hedge, mostly. That hedge is a full-time job.
B: At least she's close. Mine is in Ghana, so I just phone. It's not the same.
A: No. That's a long way.
B: It is. And I live ten minutes from Gatwick and I've never once just got on a plane. Always Christmas, always the most expensive flights. Every time I'm annoyed.
A: I've done Tenerife twice. Too hot, too many people. Passport's nearly run out. I'm not fussed.
B: So where do you go?
A: Caravan at Hunstanton. Bring the rods. Do a bit of fishing.
B: That's it? Caravan and fishing?
A: That's it. Suits me.
B: Okay, fair enough. At least you know what you like. Most people pretend they want Bali.
A: I don't want Bali.
B: No, I can see that.
A: What do you do, then? Days off.
B: Cook, mostly. Big pots at the weekend, jollof, groundnut soup, so the week is sorted. Weekdays it's fish fingers, I'm not going to lie to you.
A: Same. I do chilli in tubs. Friday's chips.
B: Friday chips here too. The kids would riot otherwise. My son says my jollof is too spicy, but I'm not changing it.
